purpose: Regression set for the scanner port. Every case is a REAL session with a known outcome and a documented reason. Not synthetic. A port that passes all of these reproduces the useful behaviour without the known defects.
usage: Replay the named session's market data and assert the expected outcome. The must_not_fire cases matter as much as the must_fire ones — they encode distinctions that took weeks to find.

must_catch.why_it_matters: Normally dormant low-float. A 250k AvgDayVolume floor excluded it; a today's-volume floor admits it. Also made NO BASE at any point, which is why the base block was deleted from the HOD filter.
tests: no base requirement on the runner filter

must_catch.why_it_matters: AvgDayVolume(20) was inflated ~4x by unadjusted historical share counts, making every ADV-normalised clause ~4x too strict on exactly the right name.
tests: no AvgDayVolume anywhere in the low-float family

must_catch.move: 1.97 prior close, ramped to 5.95, +202%, 23M shares, float under 2M
must_catch.why_it_matters: Sat between 1.73 and 2.05 for months, so ATR was ~0.12 and the old 'Last >= DayHigh - 0.15 * ATRStock' clause allowed only 2-3 CENTS. The day-range normalisation gives ~60 cents.
tests: day-high tolerance normalised to today's range, not ATR

must_catch.why_it_matters: Same stale-ATR failure as MSGY, PLUS a reverse split (54,972 print on the daily chart) distorting AvgDayVolume. Both stale references in one name.

ADV ~15M; at 15:44 the RVOL curve reads 0.92 so the denominator is ~13.8M. Dead all session plus a 2.4M spike bar gives ~10.4M cumulative -> RVOL ~0.75 against a 1.25 gate. The burst leg catches it; cumulative RVOL cannot.
The same cumulative-dilution pattern at four different times of day. Note that M_Spike_Hold still carries a BARE RVOL clause with no burst escape — the port must not reproduce that.
tests: time-local volume measure applies across ALL filters, not just the sharp-move six

must_catch.why_it_matters: ATR/price computes near 3.0%, sitting exactly on the volatility-floor boundary. Floor was lowered 0.03 -> 0.025 for this.

Continuous ramp with no pause. Also the case where a 0.25 running-low bound disqualified the whole bar after one dip, so the setup rolled to the next bar at a higher price — it fired at 179.15 when the band was 176.04.
tests: entry-timing: the fire price should not be materially above the retention band

must_catch.why_it_matters: A clean positive — fired correctly. Use as a sanity check that tightening has not broken the core case.

must_reject.why_it_matters: THE MOST IMPORTANT DISTINCTION IN THE SET. WGS and NRG held IDENTICAL positions in their spike bars — same retracement, same retention. WGS's move was already over; NRG's was still going. The separator is the LAST-MINUTE RANGE: a stock still moving has a wide final minute, a stock that has stopped has a narrow one.
tests: a last-minute range or bar-range clause distinguishes still-moving from move-over

must_reject.why_it_matters: Large caps clearing the ATR magnitude test on tiny percentage moves. The 2.5% percent floor added 2026-09-23 rejects them.
tests: percent floor of 2.5% on the spike bar

must_reject.why_it_matters: Fired on a smooth 15-minute ramp. Displacement says how FAR, never how QUICKLY — a grind produces the same number as a crash. The concentration clause (5-minute displacement >= 50% of the 15-minute displacement) rejects it.
ONE state re-firing into the evening on frozen values, not ten signals. A filter with no trigger clause and a 3-minute throttle produces this.
The gap clause compares DayBar_Open to the prior close — permanent state, true all day. An 'Open' filter with no TickTime gate runs until the close.
tests: permanent-state clauses need a time gate

must_reject.why_it_matters: STALE BREAKOUT. The monthly-level clause tests that price is above a prior-month high, which stays true for weeks after the break. Fired on a stock that had broken out long before, with no requirement that the break be recent.
tests: same-session break requirement, not merely 'above a monthly level'

must_reject.why_it_matters: 0.75% on the day is not a move. The two magnitude clauses are near-equivalent (for a stock whose ATR is 2% of price, 0.40 ATR IS 0.8% of price) so neither does independent work.
tests: membership stays well under any counter cap over a full session

must_reject.detail: 48 of 91 M_Spike_Hold fires came from 18 distinct names — JAGX x6, VKTX x6, GRML x5
must_reject.why_it_matters: A 5-minute throttle still allows six fires from one name in a session. Output volume overstates opportunity count.
tests: per-symbol session cap, or a distinct-name view in the output

unsatisfiable_at_load.defect: Last - VWAP <= -0.75 AND Last - VWAP >= 0.75 on the identical expression
unsatisfiable_at_load.expected: The loader must REJECT this at parse time with a clear message. It currently reports SET_RUNNING and has never fired.

unsatisfiable_at_load.defect: Last - VWAP = -1.25 — exact equality on a computed float
unsatisfiable_at_load.expected: The loader must WARN at parse time. Equality on a continuously-valued expression is effectively never true.

unsatisfiable_at_load.defect: Float <= 10000000 where Float is denominated in millions — the clause means 10 trillion shares
unsatisfiable_at_load.expected: A units-aware check should flag a float comparison whose magnitude implies no filtering. This same bug was fixed in one filter in August and missed in this one.

engine_behaviour_checks.name: continuous evaluation
engine_behaviour_checks.evidence: Across 98 fires from M_Drop_Sensitive_Down, timestamp seconds span the whole 0-59 range with only 4 at exactly :00.
engine_behaviour_checks.assert: Instant-true conditions are not missed by sampling. Evaluation is per-tick or near it, NOT 20-30s snapshots.

engine_behaviour_checks.name: rolling vs clock-aligned windows
engine_behaviour_checks.evidence: MinuteHigh(30, CURRENT) at 10:01 contains one minute of data. A move straddling a boundary is measured as two smaller moves — roughly one spike in five.
engine_behaviour_checks.assert: The replacement uses ROLLING windows. This is the single highest-value structural difference, and the reason several filters hand-roll windows by summing consecutive 1-minute bars.

engine_behaviour_checks.name: forming-bar range is near zero
engine_behaviour_checks.evidence: Quiet_Reversal's MinuteVolume(15,CURRENT) < MinuteVolume(15,P1) is trivially true for the first several minutes of every quarter-hour, inverting the filter's premise.
engine_behaviour_checks.assert: Any clause comparing a forming bar's RANGE or ACCUMULATING VOLUME against a completed bar is flagged at load time. Forming-bar EXTREMES (running max/min) are safe and must not be flagged.

engine_behaviour_checks.name: integer division
engine_behaviour_checks.evidence: Spike_Vol_Pct originally divided before multiplying and returned 0 on every row.
engine_behaviour_checks.assert: Arithmetic is floating-point throughout, or the loader warns on A / B * 100 where A < B is possible.

engine_behaviour_checks.name: loud failure
engine_behaviour_checks.evidence: Filters fault mid-session after repeated exceptions and are then silently disabled. A disabled filter and a quiet market look identical.
engine_behaviour_checks.assert: Any expression that faults surfaces immediately and visibly. This cost months of silent non-production on two filters.
